# Key Manager KMAC Interface — Behavioral Specification

## 1. Overview

The module is responsible for moving key-manager operation data into the KMAC engine and for returning the KMAC result once the operation completes. It supports three operation classes:

- **Advance state**
- **Identity generation**
- **Output key generation**

The module selects the data associated with the requested operation, transmits it to KMAC in fixed-width data beats, monitors the completion of the KMAC operation, and provides the resulting digest to the key manager.

The module also reports invalid-input conditions, KMAC-reported errors, command errors, and internal sequencing faults.

---

## 2. Operation Selection

The module receives separate operation-enable inputs for advance, identity generation, and output key generation.

- If no operation enable is asserted, the module shall remain idle and shall not perform any KMAC transfer.
- If exactly one operation enable is asserted, the module shall perform the corresponding operation.
- If more than one operation enable is asserted at the same time, the module shall:
  - detect a command error;
  - latch that command error until reset;
  - still execute one transaction so that the KMAC handshake completes;
  - select the transaction with a fixed priority: advance first, then identity generation, then output key generation.

Once a transaction has begun, the module shall continue that transaction to completion even if the original operation-enable conditions change.

---

## 3. Data Transfer to KMAC

The selected operation data shall be transmitted to KMAC as a sequence of fixed-width beats.

- If the selected operation data width is not an exact multiple of the KMAC beat width, the module shall zero-pad the final beat.
- The first beats of a multi-beat transfer shall carry the full data width.
- The final beat shall be marked with a last-beat indication.
- The final beat shall carry a byte strobe that marks only the bytes that contain real data. If the operation data width is an exact multiple of the beat width, the final beat shall use a full byte strobe.
- If the entire operation data fits in one beat, the module shall present that beat directly as the final beat.

The module shall hold each presented beat, including its byte strobe and last-beat indication, until KMAC accepts it. After acceptance, the module shall advance to the next beat.

While a beat is being presented, the module shall also evaluate and capture invalid-input status for the active operation. This capture shall occur even while waiting for KMAC to accept the beat.

Each time KMAC accepts a beat, the module shall assert an entropy-consumption request.

---

## 4. Operation Completion

After the final beat is accepted, the module shall wait for KMAC to report completion. The module shall not retract the transaction or start a new transaction before this completion is reported.

When KMAC reports completion:

- the module shall assert a completion indication;
- if KMAC also reports an error, the module shall assert the KMAC-error indication together with the completion indication;
- the completion indication shall remain asserted until the active operation enables are removed;
- after the operation enables are removed, the module shall clear the per-operation invalid-input status and return to idle.

The module shall present the KMAC digest result on its output while the completion indication is asserted and an operation enable is still active.

- If a sequencing fault is present, the module shall not present the KMAC digest; it shall present random decoy data instead.
- In all other conditions, including command errors, invalid-input conditions, and KMAC-reported errors, the module shall present the KMAC-produced digest so that downstream logic can determine how to handle it.
- When no completion is being reported, or when no operation enable is active, the module shall present random decoy data on the digest output rather than holding a stale value.

---

## 5. Invalid-Input Handling

The module receives invalid-input status indications associated with the supported operations. The invalid-input conditions are specific to:

- advance state;
- identity generation;
- software output generation;
- hardware output generation.

The module shall capture an invalid-input indication for the operation currently being processed.

- For an advance operation, the advance invalid-input indication shall be captured.
- For an identity-generation operation, the identity invalid-input indication shall be captured.
- For an output-key-generation operation, both the software-output and hardware-output invalid-input indications shall be captured.

Captured invalid-input status shall be held for the remainder of the transaction and shall be exposed as a single aggregated invalid-input output.

The aggregated invalid-input output shall be asserted whenever any captured invalid-input status is set. It shall remain asserted through the transaction and shall be cleared only when the operation completes and the operation enables are removed.

---

## 6. Error and Fault Reporting

The module shall provide separate error indications for different failure classes.

### 6.1 Command Error

A command error shall be detected when more than one operation enable is asserted at the same time.

Once detected, the command error shall be latched and held until reset.

While the command error is latched, the module shall substitute random decoy data for the normal operation data on every KMAC data beat. The transaction shall still run to completion so that the KMAC handshake is not left dangling.

### 6.2 Invalid Input Error

Invalid-input status shall be captured as described in Section 5.

While the aggregated invalid-input output is asserted, the module shall substitute random decoy data for the normal operation data on KMAC data beats.

This error is not permanent. It shall be cleared after the current operation finishes and the operation enables are removed.

### 6.3 KMAC-Reported Error

If KMAC reports that the operation completed with an error, the module shall propagate that condition as a KMAC-error indication together with the completion indication.

The module shall still complete its cleanup sequence and return to idle.

### 6.4 Sequencing Fault

If the internal sequencing controller ever enters an illegal state, the module shall:

- assert a sequencing-fault error indication;
- assert the completion indication;
- stop normal operation;
- present random decoy data on the digest output;
- remain in this fault state until reset.

The sequencing-fault indication is terminal and shall not be cleared by removing operation enables or by completing cleanup.

---

## 7. Reset Behavior

On reset, the module shall:

- return to idle;
- clear all transaction counters and beat state;
- deassert all completion and error indications;
- clear latched command errors;
- clear latched invalid-input status;
- stop presenting KMAC data beats;
- present random decoy data on the digest output.

---

## 8. Summary of Key Requirements

- The module shall perform one of three operation classes based on operation enables.
- It shall transfer the selected operation data to KMAC in fixed-width beats using a handshake protocol.
- It shall mark the final beat and use byte strobes to prevent invalid bytes from being transmitted.
- It shall wait for KMAC completion before reporting the operation as finished.
- It shall hold the completion indication until the operation enables are removed.
- It shall capture and report invalid-input conditions for the active operation.
- It shall substitute random decoy data on KMAC data beats whenever command-error, invalid-input, or sequencing-fault conditions are active.
- It shall report KMAC errors alongside the completion indication.
- It shall latch command errors and sequencing faults until reset.
- It shall return to idle and clear transient state after each normal completion.
